The Latest from RAND

  • Research

    How Can the United States Dominate the 6G Future?

    Nov 10, 2026

  • Video

    Inverted Rook: A New Wargame for a New Kind of Crisis

    Nov 9, 2026

  • Research

    Higher-Income Parents Use AI More and Encourage Their Children to Do the Same

    Artificial intelligence use is rising fast among U.S. parents and teens—but not equally. Higher-income parents use AI more than lower-income parents and encourage their teens to use it more, too. This could contribute to an income-based gap in teens' AI use for school or homework.

    Nov 12, 2026

  • Commentary

    Veterans, Families, and Life After Military Service: Q&A with RAND Experts

    Nov 9, 2026

  • Commentary

    Preparedness for the AI Era Requires a Reserve of Critical Workers

    Nov 4, 2026

The right research can change the world for the better.

That's why RAND is committed to solving the world's most consequential policy problems.

Learn more about RAND

Featured Research

  • Research Summary

    How—Not Just Whether—the U.S. Retrenches from Europe Matters

    Oct 28, 2026

  • Research

    Winning the Undersea Knife Fight

    Oct 20, 2026

  • Research

    China's Local Government Debt

    China's local government debt—at least $12 trillion, or 64 percent of China's GDP, in 2024—is a major fiscal challenge. What might it mean for China's economy, public services, and stability, and for U.S.-China competition?

    Oct 26, 2026

  • Teachers spend 8 hours a week supporting students' mental health and well-being.

Expert Insights

  • Parents have as vital a role as schools in helping teens navigate AI. It's not simply a question of whether students should use AI, but how they use it. Teens need guidance on when AI can support learning and when it risks doing the thinking for them.

    Heather L. Schwartz

    Vice President and Director, RAND Education, Employment, and Infrastructure

    Source: RAND News Release

  • Pain is more common among veterans than nonveterans and is associated with other serious problems like suicide and dementia. If we want to help veterans, we need to address it.

    Rajeev Ramchand

    Codirector, RAND Epstein Family Veterans Policy Research Institute

    Source: rand.org
